surveyDefinition.title: Running Shoes — consumer survey (Asia Pacific)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Running Shoes. Every question asks about Running Shoes specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Asia Pacific actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Asia Pacific who buy or use Running Shoes for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Adults who have bought running shoes for themselves in the past 12 months; Adults who run or jog regularly (at least once a week) and intend to buy running shoes in the next 6 months; Adults who consider running shoes as their primary athletic footwear for exercise. Excluded: Children under 18 (unless buying for themselves, but typically parent proxy); Professional athletes or elite runners (niche, not representative of mass market); Institutional buyers (e.g., gyms, schools, military) – not consumer segment; People who only buy running shoes for fashion without any running activity.
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Running shoes are purchased by individual consumers for personal athletic and casual use. While some running shoes are sold to institutions (e.g., for team sports), the dominant market is everyday consumers buying for themselves.
respondentBehaviours: Engages in running or jogging at least once a week
Purchases athletic footwear for fitness or casual wear
Researches product reviews and compares brands before buying
Values performance features (cushioning, support, weight) and brand reputation
May participate in running events or use fitness apps
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with running — whether they run, in what contexts, how often, and what motivates them — before narrowing to how they use their shoes across activities. It then moves through the purchase journey: what triggers a buy, how they research, where they buy, how often, what drives the final choice, and how much they spend. Next, it explores their product expectations: must-have features, fit and quality cues, style, sustainability, trade-offs, and value. It closes with satisfaction, pain points, switching triggers, recommendation intent,

targetCustomer.summary: Adult consumers of Running Shoes in Asia Pacific — who Adults who have bought running shoes for themselves in the past 12 months; Adults who run or jog regularly (at least once a week) and intend to buy running shoes in the next 6 months; Adults who consider running shoes as their primary athletic footwear for exercise. The consumer market for running shoes is broad, spanning casual joggers to serious amateurs. The audience is defined by personal use and purchase, with a focus on regular runners who are likely to have recent purchase intent. Excluding professional athletes keeps the survey representative of the mass consumer market.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes your current relationship with running?
options: I run regularly (at least once a week)
I run occasionally (a few times a month)
I run rarely (a few times a year)
I used to run but have stopped

data.label: I run regularly (at least once a week)
I run occasionally (a few times a month)
I run rarely (a few times a year)
I used to run but have stopped

questions.insight: Top response: I run regularly (at least once a week) (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mix of regular runners (Tech-Savvy, Community, Health-Motivated) and casual/occasional (Budget-Conscious, Style-Driven, Family-Focused).

questions.question: How long have you been running, in total?
questions.insight: Top response: 1 to less than 3 years (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Beginners and newer runners (Budget-Conscious, Value-Seeking) plus established runners (Health-Motivated, Community).

questions.question: When you run, who do you usually run with?
options: Mostly alone, but sometimes with others
Mostly with others, but sometimes alone

data.label: Mostly alone, but sometimes with others
Mostly with others, but sometimes alone

questions.insight: Top response: Mostly alone, but sometimes with others (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Solo running common across personas; Community Runner and Style-Driven increase group running.

questions.question: On a typical run, how far do you usually go?
questions.insight: Top response: 3–5 km (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mostly shorter distances from beginners and casual joggers; performance seekers and community runners add longer distances.

questions.question: Besides running, which of the following activities do you also use your running shoes for? Select all that apply.
options: I only use them for running

data.label: I only use them for running

questions.insight: Top response: Walking / commuting (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Family-Focused, Budget-Conscious, and Style-Driven use shoes for multiple purposes; performance-focused use only for running.

questions.question: How many pairs of running shoes do you currently own and use regularly?
questions.insight: Top response: 2 pairs (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget and value personas own fewer pairs; tech-savvy and style-driven own more.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes your main goal for running?
options: To relieve stress and clear my mind
To train for races or improve my time
To run with friends or as part of a community
To enjoy the outdoors and explore
To lose or manage my weight

data.label: To relieve stress and clear my mind
To train for races or improve my time
To run with friends or as part of a community
To enjoy the outdoors and explore
To lose or manage my weight

questions.insight: Top response: To stay fit and healthy (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-Motivated and Budget-Conscious prioritize fitness; performance and community personas drive race/community goals.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the main reason you started looking for a new pair of running shoes?
options: My current pair is worn out or damaged
I started a new fitness goal or training plan
I have an upcoming race or event
I wanted a new style or colorway
I needed a different type of shoe for a new activity

data.label: My current pair is worn out or damaged
I started a new fitness goal or training plan
I have an upcoming race or event
I wanted a new style or colorway
I needed a different type of shoe for a new activity

questions.insight: Top response: My current pair is worn out or damaged (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Worn-out shoes dominate due to budget-conscious, family-focused, and value-seeking personas; new fitness goals from beginners and health-motivated midlifers.

questions.question: Before buying a new pair of running shoes, where do you typically look for information or compare options? Select all that apply.
options: In-store staff or trying shoes on in person
None – I usually just buy what I know

data.label: In-store staff or trying shoes on in person
None – I usually just buy what I know

questions.insight: Top response: Online reviews and ratings (72.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Online research is high due to early tech adoption and value-seeking online shoppers; in-store still important for fit-focused personas.

questions.question: In the last 12 months, which of the following places have you bought running shoes from? Select all that apply.
options: Online – general retailer (e.g., department store, mass merchant)
Online – directly from a brand's website
In-store – general retailer (e.g., department store, mass merchant)

data.label: Online – general retailer (e.g., department store, mass merchant)
Online – directly from a brand's website
In-store – general retailer (e.g., department store, mass merchant)

questions.insight: Top response: In-store – general retailer (e.g., department store, mass merchant) (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: General retailers and online channels are common due to budget-conscious and value-seeking shoppers; specialist stores for performance-oriented personas.

questions.question: In the past 12 months, how many pairs of running shoes have you bought for yourself?
questions.insight: Top response: 1 pair (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Most buy 1-2 pairs; budget constraints and multi-purpose use drive lower counts, while performance and style personas buy more.

questions.question: When you are deciding between different running shoes, how much does each of the following factor into your final choice?
questions.insight: Top response: A lot (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Most factors are considered at least somewhat; price and comfort are key drivers across personas.

questions.question: Thinking about the last pair of running shoes you bought for yourself, how much did you spend?
questions.insight: Top response: $50 to $99 (34.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Price sensitivity is high; most spend under $150, with premium and tech-savvy personas pushing higher price bands.

questions.question: Thinking about your most recent purchase, which of the following best describes how you decided which running shoe to buy?
options: I bought the same model I had before without much thought
I bought the same brand but considered a different model
I researched and compared several options before deciding
I chose based on what was available in the store
I chose based on a recommendation from a friend or community

data.label: I bought the same model I had before without much thought
I bought the same brand but considered a different model
I researched and compared several options before deciding
I chose based on what was available in the store
I chose based on a recommendation from a friend or community

questions.insight: Top response: I researched and compared several options before deciding (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Research-driven decisions are common due to value-seeking and tech-savvy personas; brand-loyal personas stick with known brands.

questions.question: Which of the following features would you consider a must-have in a new pair of running shoes? Select all that apply.
options: Arch support that fits my foot
Breathable upper to keep feet cool

data.label: Arch support that fits my foot
Breathable upper to keep feet cool

questions.insight: Top response: Cushioning that absorbs impact (82.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Comfort and cushioning dominate across personas, especially Budget-Conscious Beginner, Health-Motivated Midlifer, and Family-Focused Commuter. Breathability driven by Weather-Adaptive and Metro Millennial runners. Flexible forefoot is niche, favored by Tech-Savvy Performance Seeker.

questions.question: When you are buying running shoes online, how confident are you that the size you order will fit correctly?
options: Very confident — I rarely have sizing issues
Somewhat confident — I usually get it right
Not very confident — I often worry about the fit
Not at all confident — I have had sizing problems before
I don't buy running shoes online

data.label: Very confident — I rarely have sizing issues
Somewhat confident — I usually get it right
Not very confident — I often worry about the fit
Not at all confident — I have had sizing problems before
I don't buy running shoes online

questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat confident — I usually get it right (48.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Value-Seeking Online Shopper and Digital Nomad Runner have sizing concerns, but mainstream confidence is moderate. Budget and family personas are somewhat confident due to experience. A small segment avoids online buying due to preference for local stores.

questions.question: Which of the following signs would make you trust that a running shoe is well-made and will last? Select all that apply.
options: Reinforced stitching around the toe and heel
Firm, responsive sole that springs back when pressed
High-quality materials that feel smooth and durable
A well-known brand with a strong reputation
A warranty or guarantee from the manufacturer

data.label: Reinforced stitching around the toe and heel
Firm, responsive sole that springs back when pressed
High-quality materials that feel smooth and durable
A well-known brand with a strong reputation
A warranty or guarantee from the manufacturer

questions.insight: Top response: High-quality materials that feel smooth and durable (75.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Durability cues are important to Family-Focused Commuter, Budget-Conscious Beginner, and Health-Motivated Midlifer. Reviews matter to Value-Seeking Online Shopper and Community Runner. Brand reputation is less critical for budget and value personas.

questions.question: Which of the following packaging features would you prefer for a new pair of running shoes? Select all that apply.
options: A box that can be reused or repurposed
No box, just a reusable bag

data.label: A box that can be reused or repurposed
No box, just a reusable bag

questions.insight: Top response: Minimal packaging with recyclable materials (48.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Eco-Conscious Urbanite and Style-Driven Casual Jogger prefer sustainable/reusable packaging. Budget and value personas are indifferent or prefer minimal to save cost. Standard box still chosen by those wanting protection for shipping.

questions.question: Which of the following claims would make you more likely to choose one running shoe over another? Select all that apply.
options: Made from recycled or sustainable materials
Designed and tested by professional runners
Made in a country known for quality footwear

data.label: Made from recycled or sustainable materials
Designed and tested by professional runners
Made in a country known for quality footwear

questions.insight: Top response: Designed and tested by professional runners (49.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Eco-Conscious Urbanite and Premium Luxury Enthusiast drive sustainability claims. Performance claims appeal to Tech-Savvy Performance Seeker and Community Runner. Budget and value personas are less swayed by claims unless they imply durability.

questions.question: If you had to choose between two running shoes that both fit well, which trade-off would you be most willing to make?
options: Pay more for a shoe that lasts longer
Give up some cushioning for a lighter shoe
Choose a less stylish shoe to get better performance
Choose a more sustainable shoe even if it costs more
Choose a cheaper shoe even if it wears out sooner

data.label: Pay more for a shoe that lasts longer
Give up some cushioning for a lighter shoe
Choose a less stylish shoe to get better performance
Choose a more sustainable shoe even if it costs more
Choose a cheaper shoe even if it wears out sooner

questions.insight: Top response: Pay more for a shoe that lasts longer (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Durability is top priority for Family-Focused Commuter and Budget-Conscious Beginner. Cheaper option favored by Value-Seeking Online Shopper and budget personas. Style sacrifice is acceptable to performance-focused personas, but Style-Driven Casual Jogger resists.

questions.question: For a new pair of running shoes that meets your needs, what is the highest price you would consider fair to pay?
questions.distributionNote: Price-sensitive personas (Budget-Conscious Beginner, Value-Seeking Online Shopper, Family-Focused Commuter) cluster in $50–$99. Upper-middle personas (Metro Millennial, Tech-Savvy, Premium Luxury) accept $100+. Very few go above $200.

questions.question: How much extra would you be willing to pay for a running shoe that offers noticeably better cushioning and comfort compared to a standard model?
questions.insight: Top response: Up to 10% more (34.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget and value personas are unwilling or only up to 10%. Health-Motivated Midlifer and Tech-Savvy Performance Seeker are willing to pay 11–20% for better cushioning. Premium Luxury Enthusiast may pay more than 30% for premium comfort.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied are you with the running shoes you currently use most often?
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat satisfied (36.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget-Conscious Beginners and Value-Seeking Online Shoppers (26%) skew toward dissatisfaction due to fit/price issues; Health-Motivated Midlifers and Premium Luxury Enthusiasts (14%) pull toward satisfaction.

questions.question: How satisfied are you with the durability of your current running shoes?
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat satisfied (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Durability is a pain point for Family-Focused Commuters and Metro Millennials (24%) who wear shoes heavily; Premium and Eco-conscious (10%) are more satisfied with premium materials.

questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat likely (34.00%).

storyline_notes: Added a 'shoe_rotation' beat in consumer_profile to capture multi-purpose use (running + casual + work), which is common in APAC and important for the Family-Focused Commuter and Style-Driven Casual Jogger personas.
Merged 'usage_occasion' and 'need_state' into a single 'running_context' beat to avoid overlap, and added a separate 'running_motivation' beat to capture the emotional driver.
In buying_behavior, added 'purchase_frequency' as a distinct beat to capture replacement cycle, which is more relevant than restock frequency for a durable like shoes.
In preferences_expectations, added a dedicated 'fit_and_sizing' beat because fit is a top purchase driver and a common pain point, especially for online shoppers.
Added 'style_and_colorways' beat to address the style-driven segment and the APAC trend of fashion-forward athletic footwear.
Moved 'typical_spend' later in buying_behavior to respect sensitivity, and kept 'value_expectation' last in preferences_expectations.
